Patton Village Municipal Court Address and Location

The Patton Village Municipal Court is located at: 16940 Main St, Patton Village, TX 77372, United States
Google Maps Link

This court primarily serves residents of Patton Village, including nearby areas like Splendora, Roman Forest, and Montgomery County.

Patton Village Municipal Court Working Hours

The courthouse operates on the following schedule:

  • Monday – Friday: 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM
  • Saturday – Sunday: Closed

Contact Information for Patton Village Municipal Court

Phone: 281-689-9511
Website: Patton Village Official Website

Judges and Court Staff of Patton Village Municipal Court

Judge: Ron Overman
Chief Prosecutor: Daryl D. Bailey

  • Contact: d.norton@pattonvillage.us
    Clerk of Courts: Michael Seymour, Dottie Norton

For Patton Village ticket search, case status, or general inquiries, you may reach the court clerks during office hours.

Court Jurisdiction and Types of Cases Handled at Patton Village Municipal Court

The Patton Village Municipal Court is a trial court in Montgomery County with authority over traffic violations, minor criminal cases, civil disputes, and small claims. The court handles cases like:

  • Traffic Violations: Speeding, accidents, reckless driving, etc.
  • Criminal Violations: Misdemeanors such as public intoxication and minor theft.

For more details on traffic cases, visit the Patton Village Traffic Court.

How to Search for Case Records

Patton Village Municipal Court records are accessible both online and at the county clerk’s office. For convenience, use the following methods for online search:

  • By name
  • By case number
  • By address
  • By phone or email

Note: Certain records, like criminal cases, may be restricted due to confidentiality laws. For these cases, only the individuals directly involved or authorized agencies can access information. Contact Montgomery County for further assistance with confidential records.

Traffic Violations and Fines

The Patton Village Municipal Traffic Court addresses traffic-related offenses, including speeding, DUI, and reckless driving. Failure to resolve traffic violations can lead to suspension of your driving privileges. Below is a general outline of fines:

  • 1-5 mph over speed limit: $239
  • Over 30 mph: $504
  • Non-accident violation: $210
  • Accident case: $269

For further assistance or to check if you have a Patton Village warrant, consult the warrant enforcement unit.

Plea Submission Options

If you’re issued a ticket, you can enter a plea before your court date. Options include:

  • Plea of Guilty: If you accept guilt, request a defensive driving course or deferred disposition to potentially clear the violation from your record.
  • Plea of Not Guilty: For those who contest the charges. This requires a court appearance and may involve a pre-trial with the Chief Prosecutor.

Payment Options for Fines and Tickets

You can make payments in several ways:

  1. In-Person: Pay at the courthouse with cash, check, or credit card. (Convenience fees may apply for card payments.)
  2. Online: Use the official payment portal at TrafficPayment.com by entering your ticket or citation number.
  3. By Mail: Send a certified check or money order to 16940 Main St, Patton Village, TX 77372.
  4. By Phone: Call 1-800-444-1187 to pay by credit card (service charges may apply).

Marriage License Information

Patton Village Municipal Court assists with obtaining marriage licenses through Montgomery County. Requirements include:

  • Fee: $55
  • Age: Both parties must be 18+ (under 18 requires parental/guardian consent)
  • Documentation: Original sealed birth certificate, valid photo ID, and social security number

To have the marriage ceremony at the court, schedule an appointment at least 24 hours in advance. An additional fee of $25 applies for the ceremony.

Clerk of Courts Role

The Clerk of Courts at Patton Village Municipal Court plays a critical role, managing records, processing payments, and providing various permits and licenses. They handle:

  • Marriage Licenses
  • Birth and Death Certificates
  • Permits and Warrants

For questions on licensing or case files, contact the Clerk’s Office.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

How to Contact the Licensing Department?
Call 240-777-9460 during business hours.

How to Contact the Clerk?
Visit in person during business hours or call 281-689-9511 for guidance.

Dress Code for Court?
Proper attire is required. Avoid torn, tight, or sleeveless clothing.

Can you find out if someone has a warrant? Yes, you can check if someone has a warrant by contacting the local police department or checking online databases provided by your state or county courts. In Patton Village, you can contact the Patton Village Police Department or visit their official website for information on warrants.

What is a district warrant? A district warrant is a type of arrest warrant issued by a district court. It authorizes law enforcement to arrest an individual for a specific charge and is typically used for felony offenses. The district court generally has jurisdiction over serious criminal cases within its geographical area.

What are federal warrants issued for? Federal warrants are issued for violations of federal laws. This can include serious crimes such as drug trafficking, fraud, immigration violations, and more. Federal warrants are executed by federal law enforcement agencies, such as the FBI or U.S. Marshals.

What county is Splendora, Texas in? Splendora is located in Montgomery County, Texas. It is part of the Houston metropolitan area and is close to Patton Village.

What types of cases does Patton Village Municipal Court handle?

The court handles a variety of cases, including traffic violations, minor criminal offenses, civil disputes, and small claims.

How can I find out about my court date?

You can find your court date by checking the citation you received or by contacting the Patton Village Municipal Court directly at 281-689-9511.

What are the working hours of the Patton Village Municipal Court?

The court is open Monday through Friday from 7:00 AM to 5:00 PM. The court is closed on weekends.

How do I pay my fines or fees?

Fines can be paid in person at the court, online via the court’s payment portal, or by mailing a certified check or money order to the court’s address.

Can I contest a ticket in court?

Yes, if you wish to contest a ticket, you must enter a plea of "not guilty" and appear in court on the scheduled date.

What should I expect during my court appearance?

During your court appearance, you will have the opportunity to present your case before the judge, respond to charges, and provide any evidence or witnesses you have.

How do I request a deferred disposition or defensive driving course?

You can request a deferred disposition or defensive driving course at the time of your court appearance or by contacting the court clerk in advance.

What documents do I need to bring to court?

It’s advisable to bring any relevant documents related to your case, such as the citation, identification, and any evidence or witness information you may have.

How do I obtain a copy of my case records?

You can request copies of your case records by contacting the clerk’s office at the Patton Village Municipal Court or by visiting in person during business hours.

What are the consequences of failing to appear in court?

Failing to appear in court can result in a warrant being issued for your arrest, additional fines, or other penalties.

How do I apply for a marriage license through the court?

Marriage licenses can be obtained at the clerk’s office at the Patton Village Municipal Court. Both parties must appear in person and provide necessary documentation.

What is the dress code for court appearances?

Proper attire is required for court appearances. Attendees should avoid torn, tight, or sleeveless clothing.

Can I request a public defender if I cannot afford an attorney?

You may be eligible for a public defender if you are facing criminal charges and cannot afford an attorney. This request must typically be made at your first court appearance.

What should I do if I receive a warrant for my arrest?

If you receive a warrant, it is important to contact the Patton Village Police Department or the court to address the issue promptly and avoid further legal consequences.

How can I contact the court for more information?

You can contact the Patton Village Municipal Court at 281-689-9511 during business hours or visit their official website for additional information.
